newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean troops, crowds hunt for suspected Tutsis.
newsitem.headline: Zairean troops, crowds hunt for suspected Tutsis.

text.p: Zairean troops and large crowds set up roadblocks in the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu on Thursday, hunting for suspected ethnic Tutsis ordered to leave.

"Things are becoming very ugly because of the ultimatum against the Banyamulenge," said a U.N. official of a demand by authorities that the estimated 200,000 Banyamulenge south of Bukavu leave by next Tuesday or be hunted down as rebels.
A general witch-hunt gathered pace on Thursday in this lakeside border town with indiscriminate public denunciations of suspected Banyamulenge who were then dragged off by police.

Conflict between the army and Banyamulenge, who have been denied Zairean citizenship, has been growing for months. The Banyamulenge are ethnic Tutsis who arrived in eastern Zaire up to 200 years ago from what are now Rwanda and Burundi.

Denouncing virtual war in eastern Zaire, South Kivu deputy governor Lwasi Ngabo Lwabanji on Tuesday gave the Banyamulenge a week to leave or be treated as rebels and face all-out war with Zairean soldiers.
U.N. agencies tried to evacuate more of their foreign staff from Bukavu and the town of Uvira to the south on Thursday as security worsened with Zairean troops confiscating aid agency vehicles.
But an evacuation flight to Uvira was aborted as Zairean authorities in the town refused to allow the plane to land.
Four staff from the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) were evacuated on Thursday from Bukavu on a chartered U.N. plane to the Kenyan capital Nairobi, witnesses reported.
UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg said a total of 12 U.N. and other aid agency staff were "relocated" from Uvira to Bukavu by two planes on Wednesday and 10 more might be moved on a flight on Friday.
In another development, U.N. officials were checking unconfirmed reports dozens of people were killed in an attack on Bambu village in Masisi district near the eastern Zairean town of Goma.
They said probably thousands of villagers were reported to be fleeing Bambu, which was attacked by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday night, and heading towards a Rwandan refugee camp.
They said Zairean troops posted at the camp as security were on Thursday directing the villagers to a nearby town so as not to mix up displaced Zairean families with Rwandan Hutu refugees.
In the Rwandan town of Cyangugu, which faces Bukavu, Rwanda's President Pasteur Bizimungu vowed on Thursday to bar Banyamulenge men but said his country would take women and children.
"We will be persuading the (Banyamulenge) men who are in Rwanda already to return to Zaire. Zaire needs to accept that the Banyamulenge are also Zaireans," the Hutu president added.
Rwandan and Zairean troops exchanged fire between Bukavu and Cyangugu late last month after human rights groups accused the Zairean army of carrying out atrocities against Banyamulenge.
Zairean authorities want to concentrate the Banyamulenge in government-controlled camps to make them easier to monitor.
